newsitem.title: FRANCE: French audit could show 3.6/3.7 pct deficit - paper.
newsitem.headline: French audit could show 3.6/3.7 pct deficit - paper.

text.p: An audit of French public finances due on July 21 is likely to show a 1997 public deficit running at 3.6 to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product, financial daily La Tribune said on Thursday.
The previous centre-right government, defeated in a parliamentary election on June 1, had targeted a deficit/GDP ratio of 3.0 percent in the 1997 Finance Act.

In an unsourced article, La Tribune said the audit was likely to show a central government budget deficit for this year of 3.2 percent to 3.3 percent, compared to 2.9 percent targeted by the previous government. The central government budget excludes welfare and local authority spending.
La Tribune said the welfare accounts would show a deficit of 0.6 percent of gross domestic product compared to 0.3 percent forecast by the previous government.
This would include a slight overshoot in the central social security accounts, forecast at just below 40 billion francs ($6.7 billion) rather than 30 billion francs forecast in the 1997 Finance Act.
An expected 10 billion franc surplus in national unemployment fund UNEDIC would not materialise.
Hospital investments would also knock a hole in welfare finances, the newspaper said.
The audit would show local authorities having a surplus of 0.1 percent of GDP compared to zero expected by the previous government.
It said the audit's forecast of a higher-than-expected central government budget deficit was partly due to lower than expected VAT (sales tax) revenues.
The audit would also take account of spending needs not already accounted for in the budget.
